prs.title: Fix `token_expiry_time` upon context initialization for stored tokens.
prs.author: keurcien
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both fix the same user-facing bug: an OAuthClientProvider re-initialized from stored tokens (e.g. after a process restart) fails to silently refresh an expired access token and instead forces a full interactive re-authorization. #1784 fixes the root cause directly in `_initialize()` by computing `token_expiry_time` from the stored token's `expires_in` right after loading it from storage, so `is_token_valid()` correctly reports the token as expired. #2875's own inline comment states the identical root cause verbatim ('A provider reloaded from storage never restores token_expiry_time, so is_token_valid() treats the stale token as valid and the proactive-refresh branch above is skipped') but instead patches around it by inserting a new 'Step 3.5' fallback refresh attempt inside the 401 handler of async_auth_flow before falling back to full re-authorization. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both fix the same user-facing bug: an OAuthClientProvider re-initialized from stored tokens (e.g. after a process restart) fails to silently refresh an expired access token and instead forces a full interactive re-authorization. #1784 fixes the root cause directly in `_initialize()` by computing `token_expiry_time` from the stored token's `expires_in` right after loading it from storage, so `is_token_valid()` correctly reports the token as expired. #2875's own inline comment states the identical root cause verbatim ('A provider reloaded from storage never restores token_expiry_time, so is_token_valid() treats the stale token as valid and the proactive-refresh branch above is skipped') but instead patches around it by inserting a new 'Step 3.5' fallback refresh attempt inside the 401 handler of async_auth_flow before falling back to full re-authorization. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #1784 is a 4-line fix at the actual source of the bug (missing token_expiry_time computation in _initialize) plus a new expired_tokens test fixture giving direct unit coverage of the fixed code path. #2875 is a larger change that adds a whole new branch to async_auth_flow's 401 handling as a workaround, but by its own inline comment is treating the symptom of the same unrestored-token_expiry_time defect rather than the cause, so is_token_valid() and any other caller relying on token_expiry_time remain wrong even if #2875 merges alone. Fixing #1784's root cause makes the proactive refresh path work correctly so the request would not even hit the 401 case #2875 patches, making #2875's extra branch redundant once #1784 is applied.

members.cluster_pick_reason: 2555 ships a regression test (tests/shared/test_exceptions.py) alongside the fix; 2478 has none. 2555's fix is self-contained — it adds __reduce__ directly on UrlElicitationRequiredError, reconstructing from (self._elicitations, self.message), matching the class's actual constructor. 2478 instead defines a new module-level _restore_mcp_error(exc_type, error) helper, but the posted diff never wires it into a __reduce__ call anywhere (no addition to MCPError or its subclasses invokes it) — as shown, it's dead code that doesn't fix the pickle failure by itself. 2478's only functional change is dropping a '# pragma: no cover' comment on the existing `data` property, which is cosmetic. 2555's docstring also cites the exact TypeError message and closes #2431 directly, giving higher confidence it addresses the reported bug.
